name: Black Flag
label: SST
lede: Four black bars on a thousand Hermosa Beach walls, a record label started to sell ham-radio gear, five singers in seven years, and a guitarist who never really let go.

hero.by: Henry Rollins with Black Flag, 1983. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Panic in Hermosa Beach
eras.text: Greg Ginn was a South Bay kid who ran a small ham-radio electronics business called SST. He started a fast, ugly band called Panic, his brother Raymond Pettibon renamed it Black Flag, and when nobody would put the record out, Ginn's little electronics company became SST Records.

years.h: Greg Ginn and Keith Morris start a band called Panic
years.p: Guitarist [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]] and singer [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]] form Panic in Hermosa Beach, with the Stooges and the Ramones as the blueprint. Chuck Dukowski joins on bass in 1977.

years.h: Eight songs at Media Art, with a cover band playing downstairs
years.p: Panic cut its first session at Media Art studio in Hermosa Beach while a cover band rehearsed below. Bomp! Records was interested, then ran short of cash.
years.xp:
With no label willing to pay, Greg Ginn decided to do it himself. He later said he wasn't looking forward to putting out records, and did it by default.

That default became SST Records, which went on to release [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]], [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]], [[Meat Puppets|3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf]], [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]], [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]].

years.h: Raymond Pettibon names the band and draws four black bars
years.p: Greg Ginn's brother [[Raymond Pettibon|3e603b97-d5f8-4547-891b-74cdfd2ed7bf]] suggests Black Flag, the opposite of a white flag of surrender, an anarchist banner and a can of bug spray. His logo is four black bars, a flag in mid-ripple.
years.xp:
The name change was partly to avoid confusion with another band called Panic. Pettibon went on to draw nearly every Black Flag flyer and cover of the decade, stark pen-and-ink panels that looked like they'd been torn out of a pulp novel.

The band and its fans spray-painted the bars all over Los Angeles, which is one reason the LAPD came to know the name so well.

years.h: First show as Black Flag: the Moose Lodge Hall, Redondo Beach
years.p: Black Flag's first advertised show is at a fraternal lodge in Redondo Beach. [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]] swings from the flags hanging over the stage like Tarzan.

years.h: Nervous Breakdown EP: SST 001, 2,000 copies for $1,000
years.p: Four songs in about five minutes, the first record on Greg Ginn's SST. Raymond Pettibon's cover shows a man with his back to the wall, fists up.
years.xp: According to Arthur magazine, the first pressing was 2,000 copies and cost $1,000. Henry Rollins later said the cover said it all.

yt: Black Flag live at Polliwog Park, 1979
years.h: Polliwog Park: Manhattan Beach families pelt Black Flag with food
years.p: Booked into a family concert in a Manhattan Beach park, Black Flag gets showered with food by picnicking parents. The parks department put out a press release apologizing.

years.h: Keith Morris quits and starts the Circle Jerks
years.p: [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]] leaves after the studio sessions, drinking hard and, by his own account, living on cocaine and speed. He forms the [[Circle Jerks|22995eba-1238-4b4f-a937-ac2c5767ab9f]].

years.h: Ron Reyes debuts at Blackie's, Los Angeles
years.p: [[Ron Reyes|d065eb41-b9e7-42cb-b2a5-6d211aa328e2]] already knows every song. He takes over the mic at Blackie's in Los Angeles and heads north to tour Vancouver.

eras.title: The cops, the closet and the kid from D.C.
eras.text: In two years Black Flag went through three singers, fought the LAPD in the streets and the Los Angeles Times on the page, and found the one who would define it. By the end of 1981 they had Henry Rollins, a finished album, and a record company that didn't want it.

years.h: Ron Reyes shows off his apartment: a closet at the Church
years.p: In Penelope Spheeris's The Decline of Western Civilization, [[Ron Reyes|d065eb41-b9e7-42cb-b2a5-6d211aa328e2]] gives a tour of his home, a closet in the Church, the old Hermosa Beach church Black Flag used as a practice space and crash pad.
years.xp: The Church became a hangout for South Bay punks and a regular target for Hermosa Beach police. The film was released in 1981 and did Black Flag's reputation for chaos no harm at all.

years.src: Center Label show list · Arthur · Wikipedia
years.h: Ron Reyes quits mid-set at the Fleetwood
years.p: Fed up with the violence at shows, [[Ron Reyes|d065eb41-b9e7-42cb-b2a5-6d211aa328e2]] walks off the stage at the Fleetwood in Redondo Beach. Audience members take turns at the mic; Reyes comes back, then quits for good.
years.xp:
Arthur's history says Reyes snapped after his girlfriend got shoved around in the crowd. Black Flag had just recorded the Jealous Again EP with him, released later in 1980 with Reyes credited as Chavo Pederast.

Reyes moved to Vancouver and formed Crash Bang Crunch Pop! He'd be back 33 years later.

years.h: The Los Angeles Times: 'Violence Sneaks Into Punk Scene'
years.p: A Los Angeles Times feature ties Black Flag to punk violence. For the LAPD under Chief Daryl Gates, the band becomes public enemy number one, and shows start getting shut down on sight.
years.xp:
The band's 'Police Story' single art, a cop with a gun barrel in his mouth, went up as flyers all over town. A Hermosa Beach officer told Chuck Dukowski there was a stack of law books from there to the beach, per Arthur.

On NBC's Tomorrow show, Dukowski had to explain that Black Flag were not white supremacists.

years.h: Dez Cadena becomes Black Flag's third singer
years.p: [[Dez Cadena|f3cd8685-7490-44ee-a5bd-cc6663ea1396]] takes the mic. He sings on the Six Pack EP and the band's version of Louie Louie.

years.h: Hermosa Beach police raid SST while Black Flag is on tour
years.p: With the band away, police raid the SST office. [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] of [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]], who was there, gets hit with a $50 zoning citation.
years.xp:
At Baces Hall in East Hollywood the same year, police showed up with a command post and a helicopter overhead. Black Flag's solution was to book wherever it could: picnics, house parties, schools, and halls far from Hollywood.

On tour the per diem was five dollars at most, often nothing. Greg Ginn's father brought sandwiches.

years.h: Henry Rollins, a D.C. ice-cream shop manager, jumps on the mic at A7
years.p: [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]], singer of D.C.'s [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]] and a manager at a Häagen-Dazs, gets up to sing with Black Flag at an after-show party at A7 in New York. Days later they ask him to join.
years.xp: Dez Cadena's voice was shot from screaming every night, and he wanted to play guitar. Rollins quit his job, met the band in July, and roadied the rest of the tour, coming out to sing the encores.

years.src: Center Label show list · Ultimate Guitar
years.h: Henry Rollins's first show as singer: the Cuckoo's Nest, Costa Mesa
years.p: Henry Rollins, 20, fronts Black Flag for the first time at the Cuckoo's Nest in Costa Mesa. Dez Cadena moves to rhythm guitar.

years.h: Damaged: $8,500, under three weeks, a fist through a mirror
years.p: Black Flag's first album, cut at Unicorn Studios in West Hollywood, with 'Rise Above', 'TV Party' and 'Six Pack'. Ed Colver's cover shows Henry Rollins punching a mirror.
years.xp: Arthur puts the budget at $8,500. The 'blood' on the cover was red ink and coffee. Kurt Cobain later put Damaged in his personal top 50.

q: I found it an anti-parent record, past the point of good taste.
years.h: MCA refuses to distribute Damaged, calls it 'anti-parent'
years.p: MCA's Al Bergamo pulls distribution through Unicorn Records. Black Flag puts his words on a sticker on 25,000 copies and sells the record through independents.
years.xp:
MCA refused distribution in September 1981. Bergamo said the record bothered him and was past the point of good taste; Wikipedia notes the real problem may have been how badly Unicorn was being run.

Unicorn sued for breach of contract and won an injunction that stopped the band from releasing records under the name Black Flag.

years.h: Robo stranded after the UK tour by visa trouble
years.p: Colombian-born drummer [[Robo|6dc378d0-6465-45d3-8b5a-918e2c19b278]] can't legally get back into the US after Black Flag's December 1981 UK tour. He later drums for the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]].

eras.title: A band barred from its own name
eras.text: Black Flag spent two years unable to put out a record called Black Flag. Drummers came and went, and the band got slower, heavier and meaner in the practice room while the lawyers argued.

years.h: Three drummers in one year: Emil Johnson, Chuck Biscuits, Bill Stevenson
years.p: Sixteen-year-old Emil Johnson quits mid-tour after a fight with roadie Mugger. [[Chuck Biscuits|2ba59002-1ff3-4f53-87aa-6a085acf15e2]] of [[D.O.A.|0f0b2f97-a073-4a92-ab99-ff7980ad7fca]] balks at the rehearsal schedule. [[Bill Stevenson|328e3ae5-7d8c-4a01-b2b3-b8f41fb7bb23]] of the [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]] sticks.

years.h: Greg Ginn and Chuck Dukowski go to jail for contempt of court
years.p: Unicorn's injunction holds, and Greg Ginn and Chuck Dukowski each serve time in Los Angeles County Jail for contempt. The case dies only when Unicorn goes bankrupt.

years.h: Everything Went Black: a Black Flag album without the name
years.p: Old recordings with all three pre-Rollins singers, credited to the members' names because the band couldn't legally use its own.

years.h: Dez Cadena leaves to form DC3
years.p: [[Dez Cadena|f3cd8685-7490-44ee-a5bd-cc6663ea1396]] quits to start his own band, DC3. He isn't replaced; Black Flag goes on with one guitar.

years.h: Chuck Dukowski is out of the band he helped build
years.p: Greg Ginn wants a new direction, and per Wikipedia it falls to Henry Rollins to tell Chuck Dukowski. Dukowski stays on as manager and booking agent.

years.h: Kira Roessler joins on bass
years.p: L.A. punk veteran [[Kira Roessler|2c65be73-5658-47c5-9619-01f78db0e2cb]] joins just after the My War sessions, where Greg Ginn played bass himself.

eras.title: Slower, longer, meaner
eras.text: Free of Unicorn, Black Flag released six records in about 18 months and toured without end. Side two of My War slowed hardcore to a crawl, lost them half their audience and helped plant grunge.

years.h: My War: side two crawls, and grunge takes notes
years.p: Greg Ginn plays bass as 'Dale Nixon'. Side two is three songs over six minutes each: 'Nothing Left Inside', 'Three Nights' and 'Scream'.
years.xp:
Recorded in December 1983 at Total Access in Redondo Beach. Chuck Dukowski still wrote the title track and 'I Love You'.

Hardcore kids hated the slow side. [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]]'s Steve Turner has credited it with pushing the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] to slow down, and grunge followed.

years.h: Kurt Cobain's first punk show: Black Flag on the My War tour
years.p: [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] sees his first punk show at a Black Flag show on the My War tour. [[Mark Arm|3f99d2df-8859-4249-8a70-84fe04c5a096]] says a 1983 Black Flag show moved him to tears.

years.h: Family Man: one side Henry Rollins poetry, one side instrumentals
years.p: Black Flag's oddest record splits into Henry Rollins spoken word and Greg Ginn-led instrumentals. Ginn later said Rollins had gone into the serious way-out poet thing.

years.h: Slip It In, and a Raymond Pettibon cover people still argue about
years.p: The third Black Flag album of 1984, with Kira Roessler on bass and Bill Stevenson on drums. Pettibon's cover drawing is one of his most provocative.

years.h: Greg Ginn fires Bill Stevenson; Anthony Martinez takes the drums
years.p: [[Bill Stevenson|328e3ae5-7d8c-4a01-b2b3-b8f41fb7bb23]] goes back to the [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]]. Anthony Martinez replaces him.

years.h: Loose Nut ends in a fight with Raymond Pettibon
years.p: Greg Ginn reuses a Raymond Pettibon drawing for the Loose Nut cover without asking. The brothers stop speaking for a time.

years.h: Kira Roessler out, C'el Revuelta in on bass
years.p: Wikipedia says [[Kira Roessler|2c65be73-5658-47c5-9619-01f78db0e2cb]] was fired. She later marries [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] and records with him as Dos.

years.h: In My Head: the last Black Flag studio album for 28 years
years.p: Metal-heavy and blues-bent, cut by Greg Ginn, Henry Rollins, Kira Roessler and Bill Stevenson before the lineup broke apart.

years.h: Last show: Detroit, June 27, 1986
years.p: The final tour, January to June with C'el Revuelta and Anthony Martinez, ends in Detroit. Nobody announces it's the end.

q: I thought that was strange considering it was his band and all.
years.h: Greg Ginn calls Henry Rollins to say he's quitting
years.p: Greg Ginn phones Henry Rollins and says he's leaving Black Flag. That's the breakup.
years.xp: Rollins has written that by 1986 Ginn was inseparable from his Anvil case and a large marijuana stash. Rollins started the [[Rollins Band|3ca37f23-fdce-49ce-86e2-134c9a17ebc5]] within months.

eras.title: The van becomes a book
eras.text: Black Flag's story got told from the back of the van. Henry Rollins's tour diary won a Grammy, and Greg Ginn briefly revived the band for a cause close to his heart: cats.

years.h: Henry Rollins publishes Get in the Van
years.p: Henry Rollins's diary of 1981 to 1986: violent shows, endless driving, police abuse. The audiobook wins the Grammy for Best Spoken Word Album in 1995.

years.h: A Black Flag reunion to benefit cat rescue
years.p: Greg Ginn, Dez Cadena, Robo and C'el Revuelta play two Hollywood Palladium shows and one at Alex's Bar in Long Beach for a cat rescue. Skater [[Mike Vallely|686467eb-5399-4c43-adbe-dad0e059c738]] sings all of My War.

eras.title: Two Black Flags and a lawsuit
eras.text: Thirty years on, two bands claimed the bars: Greg Ginn's Black Flag and FLAG, made of nearly everyone else. It ended up in federal court, and Ginn's new singer got fired in front of an audience.

years.h: Keith Morris, Chuck Dukowski and Bill Stevenson play Nervous Breakdown
years.p: At Goldenvoice's 30th anniversary show in Santa Monica, [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]], Chuck Dukowski, Bill Stevenson and [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]] guitarist Stephen Egerton play the whole Nervous Breakdown EP.

years.h: Greg Ginn and Ron Reyes announce a new Black Flag
years.p: Greg Ginn reforms Black Flag with [[Ron Reyes|d065eb41-b9e7-42cb-b2a5-6d211aa328e2]] back on vocals. The same week, Morris, Dukowski, Stevenson and Egerton announce FLAG, later joined by [[Dez Cadena|f3cd8685-7490-44ee-a5bd-cc6663ea1396]].

years.h: Greg Ginn and SST sue FLAG, Henry Rollins and Keith Morris
years.p: SST and Ginn sue over the name and the four bars, and move to cancel trademark filings Henry Rollins and Keith Morris made in 2012.
years.xp: In October 2013 a federal judge refused Ginn's request for a preliminary injunction, found the logo might be in generic use, and ruled fans could tell Black Flag and FLAG apart.

years.h: Mike Vallely takes Ron Reyes's mic mid-set in Perth
years.p: On tour in Australia, manager [[Mike Vallely|686467eb-5399-4c43-adbe-dad0e059c738]] grabs Ron Reyes's microphone, orders him offstage and sings the last two songs himself. Reyes said he felt relief.

years.h: What The...: the first Black Flag album since 1985
years.p: Greg Ginn and Ron Reyes's comeback album lands to poor reviews.

years.h: Mike Vallely named singer; Greg Ginn shelves the band after one tour
years.p: After the Victimology Tour with Tyler Smith and Brandon Pertzborn, Ginn dissolves Black Flag again.

eras.title: Tacos, My War and a new voice
eras.text: Greg Ginn kept bringing the bars back, now as a band of players decades younger than him. The original run's rawest record became a nightly set, and in 2025 the band got its first woman singer.

years.h: Black Flag returns at a craft beer and taco festival in Dana Point
years.p: After five years away, Greg Ginn and Mike Vallely come back at the Sabroso Craft Beer, Taco & Music Festival. A UK tour follows in October, the first in 35 years.

years.h: Black Flag plays My War start to finish
years.p: The 2023 North American tour plays the 1984 My War album in full, slow side and all.

years.h: Mike Vallely quits after almost 11 years
years.p: [[Mike Vallely|686467eb-5399-4c43-adbe-dad0e059c738]] leaves after a run of North American shows.

years.h: Max Zanelly becomes Black Flag's first woman singer
years.p: Greg Ginn's new lineup: Max Zanelly on vocals, David Rodriguez on bass, Bryce Weston on drums. The next month FLAG plays Punk Rock Bowling.
